preamble: A palatalized bilabial nasal [mʲ] can lose its labial closure and keep only the palatal component, giving the palatal nasal [ɲ]. This is part of the wider pattern of labial palatalization, in which [pʲ bʲ mʲ] become [c ɟ ɲ]. It is found in the Moldavian dialect of Romanian (miel 'lamb' pronounced [ɲʲel]), in Aromanian, where Latin m before a front vowel gives nj [ɲ] (njadzã 'middle' beside Romanian miază), and in Lhasa Tibetan, where the Old Tibetan palatalized onset [mʲ] (written my-) is pronounced [ɲ].

examples.note: Labials before front vowels are palatalized and become [c ɟ ɲ]: copil 'child' [koˈkʲil], bine 'well' [ˈɡʲini], miel [ɲʲel].

examples.from: Latin media, Proto-Romanian palatalized *mʲ (cf. Romanian miază)
examples.note: Aromanian ⟨nj⟩ spells [ɲ]; the palatalized labial lost its lip closure.
The palatalized labial onset (written my-) is pronounced as a palatal nasal in the modern Lhasa language.
